subject: Incident taxonomy v1 — review + sign-off (target rollout 12/16)
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Dec 5, 2025 at 4:12 PM
Subject: Incident taxonomy v1 — review + sign-off (target rollout 12/16)

Team —

We’re ready for cross-team sign-off on Incident taxonomy v1 (types/subtypes + ownership mapping + remediation SLAs). Goal is to roll this into incident-bot + dashboards starting the week of 12/16.

Links:
- Taxonomy definitions + decision tree: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/Incident+taxonomy+v1+definitions
- Ownership mapping + remediation SLA matrix: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/Incident+ownership+mapping+and+remediation+SLA+matrix
- Incident classification policy update (close gating, “unknown” rules): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ONCALL/Incident+classification+policy
- Tracking ticket for rollout: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/incident-taxonomy-v1-proposal-and-review

Attached: a short review pack (tables + open questions in one place).

Asks (please reply inline):
1) Approval to publish v1 as “required field” starting 12/16.
2) Any blockers on the remediation SLA defaults by tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and severity.
3) Confirm we’re aligned on the last open questions below:
   a) Capacity vs routing ownership in overload scenarios: when do we call it “Capacity shortage” vs “Routing/fallback misbehavior”?
   b) Cloud provider / region-wide events: explicit carve-out language for SLA timers (pause vs not-applicable).
   c) Metrics labeling: incident_type low-cardinality allowlist + Unknown/Unclassified bucket for first 2 weeks.

If you’re good with v1 as-is, a +1 is sufficient.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Executive Sponsor, SRE
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Incident_Taxonomy_v1_Review_Pack_2025-12-05.pdf


---

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 8, 2025 at 9:03 AM
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy v1 — review + sign-off (target rollout 12/16)

+1 to rolling out 12/16.

Two notes on (a) capacity vs routing ownership:
- I agree with the current rule of thumb in the decision tree: if fallback is behaving per policy (and we’re just out of headroom), it’s Capacity shortage (primary Fleet/Infra). If fallback is not occurring or is oscillating/incorrect target selection, it’s Routing/fallback misbehavior (primary Routing/Control Plane).
- Please make sure the “overload” symptom doesn’t default to Routing. We had a couple Q3 incidents where the router did its job but there simply wasn’t capacity in-region.

Also: for carve-outs (b), I’d prefer we don’t create a big “not applicable” escape hatch. If we pause the SLA timer, there should be a required reason + approver (IC + SRE on-call) in incident-bot.

-Ava


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 8, 2025 at 10:41 AM
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy v1 — review + sign-off (target rollout 12/16)

I’m supportive of the 12/16 rollout.

On remediation SLAs: Dedicated is the sensitive one for comms. The current matrix looks reasonable as long as:
- “Time-to-mitigate” is what we alert/push operationally (and what we show to CS internally), and “time-to-fix” is tracked but not used as a customer-facing promise by default.
- Region-wide / cloud-provider events: agree with Ava that “pause with reason + approval” is better than “N/A.” We need consistency for post-incident reviews.

One request: can we add a single line to the policy that Dedicated incidents should default to proactive customer comms for Sev0/Sev1 once classified? (Even if status page language stays generic.)

Lauren
Product, Dedicated


---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 8, 2025 at 12:18 PM
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy v1 — review + sign-off (target rollout 12/16)

+1 from me with two small tweaks to reduce churn later:

1) Naming: In the taxonomy table, can we make sure “Control plane outage” includes config write failures and policy propagation stalls (so Support doesn’t bounce between categories). I saw the “Control plane — API degradation” subtype; I think we should explicitly mention “policy updates failing / stuck” in examples.

2) Console surfacing: For the first release, I’d recommend we treat incident_type/subtype as ops-only in Console and let CS view read-only (no editing). That avoids the “different classification in different places” problem.

Everything else looks good.

Marissa


---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 8, 2025 at 5:26 PM
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy v1 — review + sign-off (target rollout 12/16)

Approved to proceed with v1 and make taxonomy required starting 12/16.

Conditions / expectations:
- Keep v1 low-cardinality as proposed. Don’t add new top-level types during rollout week; capture gaps for v1.1.
- “Unknown/Unclassified” is acceptable for the first two weeks but should trend down; please report weekly classification compliance to this group.
- SLA pause: agree with the direction here—require a reason + SRE approval. We need this auditable.

Please ensure the policy is explicit on who can change incident_type during an incident (IC + primary on-call), and that the final classification is reviewed in postmortem.

Neha


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, Dec 9, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy v1 — review + sign-off (target rollout 12/16)

Thanks all — captured the edits and we’ll fold them into the v1 publish today.

Plan (so we’re aligned):
- Update definitions page with Marissa’s control plane example language (“policy update failures / stuck propagation”).
- Update policy to explicitly state: IC + primary on-call can set/change incident_type; final classification reviewed in postmortem.
- Add SLA pause workflow: incident-bot requires pause_reason + SRE on-call approval (and logs it).
- Dedicated comms note: we’ll add a policy line that Sev0/Sev1 Dedicated defaults to proactive CS outreach once classification is set.

Rollout target remains 12/16 (incident-bot gating + dashboards). We’ll keep v1 stable and log v1.1 candidates as we see Unknowns.

I’ll send the “go live” note + short training snippet to on-call leads later this week.

Sean


---

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Dec 9, 2025 at 11:07 AM
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy v1 — review + sign-off (target rollout 12/16)

Sounds good. One last request: in the decision tree, can you add a single “check fallback_reason metrics first” step before people pick Routing vs Capacity? That should reduce the back-and-forth in the incident channel.

Otherwise +1.

-Ava
